question: Refer to the exhibit. A traffic collector virtual machine is installed inside the Cisco UCS server. The collector must monitor traffic that is received on G1/2 with ERSPAN. Which set of actions must be taken to send the traffic to the traffic collector?
context: Topology: SW1 (G1/2) connects to FI-A and FI-B, which connect to the UCS Chassis containing the collector VM.
imageNote: Diagram: a red-highlighted client connects to SW1 (G1/2), which connects to FI-B and FI-A; both FI-B and FI-A connect down to the UCS Chassis (red ERSPAN traffic path highlighted).
options: Configure ERSPAN. Configure a source session on Cisco UCS Manager.
Configure SPAN. Configure a source session on the SW1 switch.
Configure SPAN. Configure a source session on Cisco UCS Manager.
Configure ERSPAN. Configure a source session on the SW1 switch.
explanation: Community-voted answer (B) conflicts with the marked correct answer (D); presented as officially marked (D).
theory: Local SPAN can only mirror traffic to a destination on the same switch as the monitored port; to send a copy of traffic monitored on switch SW1's port G1/2 to a destination VM sitting behind the UCS fabric interconnects (a different device, reachable only over the network), the traffic must instead be encapsulated and routed using ERSPAN, which tunnels mirrored frames over IP to a remote destination. Because the monitored port (G1/2) physically resides on SW1, the ERSPAN source session must be configured on SW1 itself — not on Cisco UCS Manager, which has no visibility into that upstream switch port. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 12 — Cisco UCS Traffic Monitoring, ERSPAN vs. Local SPAN)
